newsitem.title: USA: Int'l, large cap funds continue flow strength -AMG.
newsitem.headline: Int'l, large cap funds continue flow strength -AMG.

text.p: Money flowing into large capitalization growth mutual funds and international funds continued to be strong for the week ended April 23, according to AMG Data Services.
The fund-tracking firm, based in Arcata, California, said that flows into the large-cap growth sector rose to $418 million compared to $84 million for the week of April 16.
Flows into international funds remained strong at $615 million versus $618 million fore the previous week, according to AMG.

The money flowing into the sector was the highest since early March, said AMG president Robert Adler. He said he believed that the continued strength of the U.S. dollar was partially responsible for the popularity of the sector.
The emerging growth -- or small-cap -- sector had marginal inflows of about $17 million versus redemptions of $296 million the previous week.
The aggressive growth sector -- which includes large, medium and small-cap -- had outflows of $10 million compared to inflows of $48 million.
"Clearly investor sentiment is directed toward larger cap and international funds," Adler said.

Adler said that about $2.5 billion in new cash came into all equity funds for the most recent week, compared to $1.6 billion for the previous period, but far below the $4.7 billion for the week a year ago.
Based on the monthly data to date, Adler said he expected the April flows to be "significantly lighter than April a year ago."
